clip.title: Fire Drill
clip.dialogue:
*door shuts* *locks door* Last {{blank}} I give a fire safety talk, *clears throat* and nobody paid any attention.
It's my own fault for using PowerPoint. PowerPoint is boring. People learn in lots of different {{blank}}, but experience is the best teacher.
*pours lighter fluid* *lights cigarette* Today, smoking is {{blank}} save lives.
*flicks cigarette, igniting trash bin* *throws lighter fluid container into fire*
Does anyone smell anything smoky? Did you bring your {{blank}} in again?
*clears throat* Oh my God! Uh.. Oh my God! Stanley: FIRE!
Oh Fire?! Oh my goodness! What's the {{blank}}? What do we do people? The phones are dead! Dwight: Oh how did that happen? Kevin: It's out in the {{blank}}!
Dwight: No, we don't know that. The smoke can {{blank}} coming {{blank}} an air duct. Michael: Oh my God! Okay, it's happening! Everybody stay {{blank}}! Dwight: What's the procedure everyone? What's the procedure? Michael: STAY F*****G CALM!
Dwight: Wait, wait, wait, wait, wait! Michael: {{blank}} F*****G CALM DOWN!! Dwight: No no! Michael No! Dwight: Touch the handle, if it's hot, there could be a fire in the {{blank}}!
Michael: What does warm mean? Everyone: *groaning* Oh my God. Dwight: Mmm, not a {{blank}} option. Dwight: What next? Michael: Don't Run!
Everyone: *Murmuring in Panic* Dwight: Oh! Here's a door. Check that one out. How's the {{blank}}? Andy: It-- it's warm! Jim: K--go to the back door. Dwight: Well, uh, another option.
*Everyone panicking and screaming* Dwight: {{blank}}! Ok! {{blank}} down everyone. No bunching! Phyllis: Oh! I forgot my {{blank}}. Andy: Leave it woman! Michael: Get out of the way! Go, go, go!
Dwight: Things can be replaced, Phyllis! People, human {{blank}}, however, can- *Chaos and Panic* Oscar: Ah! My hand! That's hot!
Andy: Aah! This ones hot too! Michael: Okay, we're {{blank}}. Everyone for himself. Dwight: Okay, let's go. Everyone: *shouting* Out of my way! Let's go. Get out of my way!
*Chaos and Panic* Dwight: Calm, please Andy: Get out of the way! Dwight: Have you ever seen a {{blank}} victim? Andy: Move it!! Dwight: Okay! Procedure, procedure. Exit options. Where do we go {{blank}}? Wha-- Use a what to cover the mouth?
*MORE Chaos and Panic* Angela: *pulling cat out of filing drawer* It's okay. Shh shhh.
*cat meows* Dwight: A what? A {{blank}}. A damp rag perhaps.
*Oscar escaping through roof* Dwight: Let's remember those procedures. What are the options?
*Pushing and Shoving* Dwight: Okay, that's the wrong way. {{blank}} tried that. Dwight: Remember your exit points. Exit points people. Angela: Oscar. Oscar!
Oscar: Stay alive! I'm getting help! Angela: Pull me up! Oscar: You're too heavy! Angela: I only {{blank}} 82 pounds!
*Oscar crawls away* Angela: Uh-- save Bandit!
Angela: *throws cat into air duct and he falls out through the other side* *MEOW* Angela: OH! Dwight: How about 911? Anyone? 911.
Michael: *tries to break open window* *SMACK* Kevin: *smashes vending machine with a chair* *steals snacks*
*SMASH* Pam: What do we do?! Dwight: Use the {{blank}} of fear and adrenaline to sharpen your decision-making. Jim: Okay, I am not dying here. Come on.
*Dwight lights firecrackers* *Mass Coughing* *Firecrackers pop loudly* Angela: What is that? What is that? Andy: THE FIRE'S {{blank}} AT US!!
*Everyone Screaming* Phyllis: What in the name of God is going on?!
*Dwight pulls Fire Alarm* Jim: Let's try this Andy: Yes! Yes, ba-- Yes, {{blank}} ram! Battering ram!
*Oscar's leg crashes through the ceiling* Phyllis and Creed: Ahhhh!!! Andy: Go, go, go, go, go!! AHHH!
*Jim and Andy ram the door with the copying machine* *Angela shrieks* *Everyone yelling* *Micheal throws projector out window* Micheal: HELP!! HELP!!
Stanley: Oh God! I'm {{blank}} to die!
*Jim and Andy ram the door with the copying machine* *Everyone shrieking* *Dwight blows airhorn* Dwight: ATTENTION!! Dwight: Employees of {{blank}}!
Dwight: This has been a test of our emergency preparedness. Dwight: There is no fire. It was only a {{blank}}. Jim: WHAT?!
Dwight: Fire not real. This was merely a training exercise.
*Oscar drops down from ceiling* Dwight: So what have we learned?
*Stanley collapses* Dwight: Oh come on! It's not real Dwight: Stanley don't have a {{blank}} attack! *everyone rushes to Stanley* Michael: No, no, no! You will not {{blank}}! Stanley! Michael: STANLEY YOU WILL NOT DIE!
Michael: Stanley! Stanley! Michael: Barack is President! Michael: YOU ARE BLACK STANLEY!
Michael: I'm gonna give him mouth-to-mouth Jim: No, no, no! Don't give him mouth to mouth for this! Michael: He's going to {{blank}} his tongue. Jim: No. Michael. Michael. Michael: Don't swallow it! Kelly: Michael get off him! Stop!
Michael: I'm fine! Leave me al-- *Michael bring dragged away by Toby, Kevin, and Jim* *Outro*

words.translation: to set something on fire or cause it to start burning
words.example: Today, smoking is going to save lives.

words.translation: a hormone your body releases that gives you extra energy in fear or danger
words.example: Use the power of fear and adrenaline to sharpen your decision-making.

words.translation: the state of being ready to handle an emergency or difficult situation
words.example: This has been a test of our emergency preparedness.

words.translation: only; nothing more than — used to make something sound less important
words.example: This was merely a training exercise.

words.translation: crowding together in one tight group — usually blocks movement in an emergency
a tube or channel that carries air, water or wires through a building
words.example: The smoke could be coming from an air duct.

words.translation: a heavy object used to break down a door by force — here, a copy machine
to make food or liquid go down your throat — or, in a panic, your own tongue
words.example: He is going to swallow his tongue.

questions.question: Why does Dwight decide to start a fire in the office?

options.text: He wants to show everyone that PowerPoint is very boring.
He strongly believes that real experience is the best teacher.
He secretly thinks everyone needs to leave the office early.
He accidentally drops his lit cigarette into the garbage bin.

questions.correctAnswer: He strongly believes that real experience is the best teacher.

questions.question: What is Dwight's specific advice when touching the door handle?

options.text: If it is hot, there could be a fire in the main hallway.
If it is warm, you should open the heavy door carefully.
If it is cold, you must stay inside the conference room.
If it is locked, you have to break the nearest glass window.

questions.correctAnswer: If it is hot, there could be a fire in the main hallway.

questions.question: What does Michael tell everyone to do when they realize they are trapped?

options.text: They must follow all of Dwight's official emergency procedures.
They should wait patiently for the local firefighters to arrive.
They have to find some damp rags to cover their faces quickly.
They are trapped and it is every man for himself at this point.

questions.correctAnswer: They are trapped and it is every man for himself at this point.

questions.question: What heavy object do Jim and Andy use as a battering ram?

options.text: They pick up a heavy snack vending machine.
They use the large office copying machine.
They grab a large wooden conference table.
They push the metal filing cabinet drawer.

questions.correctAnswer: They use the large office copying machine.

questions.question: Where does Angela try to save her cat, Bandit, during the chaos?

options.text: She puts him inside the bottom metal filing drawer.
She carries him safely through the main front door.

slides.title: Language focus: Modal verbs for possibility and deduction

words.translation: use this to say something is possibly happening right now — uncertain present
words.example: The smoke can be coming from an air duct.

words.translation: use this to express a possible explanation for something you observe
words.example: Touch the handle, if it's hot, there could be a fire in the hallway!

words.translation: use 'can' with a past participle to talk about what is possible in general

slides.content:
In this scene, characters use modal verbs to talk about what is possible, likely, or deduced from evidence. Modals like 'could' and 'can' help speakers express degrees of certainty without stating facts.
• 'Could' expresses possibility — the speaker is not certain but thinks something is likely ('The smoke could be coming from an air duct.').
• 'Can' in this context signals a logical consequence — if a condition is met, something is able to happen ('There could be a fire in the hallway.').
• Modals are always followed by the base form of the verb — never add -s, -ed, or -ing to the verb directly after the modal.
Whenever you're not 100% sure about something you observe, reach for a modal — just like Dwight does when he is trying to deduce where the fire is coming from.

slides.title: Over to you
slides.content:
Read the Room — You walk into a place — the office, a classroom, your house — and something feels off. Nobody is talking, or the door is locked, or people look nervous. Tell me about a time this happened. What did you think was going on before you knew for sure?
The Overreaction — Think of a moment when someone at work, school or home turned a small problem into total chaos. What do you think was really behind their reaction — stress, something personal, something they were trying to prove?
Steal a Line — Pick one line from the scene you'd love to drop into your week — a meeting, a chat with your family, a group chat. Where would it fit, and how would people react?
slides.prompt: The chaos is over — now think about a time your world went sideways and tell me what was really going on underneath.
